7. A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0.
B. 𝑣0 cos 𝜃.
C. 𝑣0 sin 𝜃.
D. 0.
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
Q7. A tennis ball is launched with speed \(v_0\) at an angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal (ignore air resistance). What is the ball’s speed at its maximum height?
A. \(v_0\).
This is incorrect because the vertical component decreases to zero at the top, so the speed is reduced from \(v_0\).
B. \(v_0\cos\theta\).
This is correct because at maximum height the vertical velocity is zero and the horizontal component remains \(v_0\cos\theta\).
C. \(v_0\sin\theta\).
This is incorrect because \(v_0\sin\theta\) is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at the top.
D. 0.
This is incorrect because the horizontal component of velocity is generally nonzero at the maximum height.

This is incorrect because the acceleration depends on t due to the t3 term in position.

This is incorrect because 1.90 m/s2 is a position coefficient, not the constant acceleration.

12. A 4.5 kg cart initially moving at 2.1 m/s collides with a wall and rebounds at a speed of 1.3 m/s moving backward. The collision lasts for 0.2 seconds. What is the average force exerted on the cart during the collision?

B. 18 N.
C. 76.5 N.

A. 17.1 N
This is incorrect because it uses only the rebound speed rather than the full change in velocity (including the reversal of direction).
B. 38.4 N
This is incorrect because it effectively uses an incorrect Δv that does not account for the sign change properly.

D. None of the above is correct
This is incorrect because option C correctly computes the average force magnitude from impulse.

This is incorrect because the escape-speed formula depends on the planet’s M and R, not on the escaping object’s mass.
B. Escape speed is higher on a planet with smaller mass and larger radius.
This is incorrect because decreasing M and increasing R both reduce GM/R, lowering escape speed.
C. If a planet’s mass and radius are both cut in half, the escape speed must be smaller.
This is incorrect because M/R stays the same when both are scaled by the same factor, so the escape speed is unchanged.
D. Escape speed is higher on a planet with greater mass and smaller radius.
This is correct because increasing M and decreasing R increases GM/R, which increases v.

Q13. A 65 kg catcher is initially at rest. A 145 g baseball traveling at 90 mph is caught and sticks in the catcher’s mitt. What is the catcher’s speed immediately after the catch?

This is incorrect because it comes from mishandling the mph-to-m/s conversion or not dividing by the combined mass correctly.

This is incorrect because it assumes the catcher ends up moving nearly as fast as the ball despite the catcher’s much larger mass.
D. 2.0 × 10−4 m/s
This is incorrect because it over-divides by mass (typically from using grams as kilograms or adding an extra factor of 1000).
